text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. Vice President Al Gore, on a 4-day visit to Beijing, called for new structures of cooperation and communication among world's powers.
- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong assures Laos Singapore will support Vientiane's economic reforms and welcomes the country as member of ASEAN along with Cambodia and Burma.
- Brunei and Singapore say they have no intention of terminating an agreement that allows their currencies to be exchanged on a one-to-one basis.
- New paging operators M1, ST Messaging and Hutchinson IntraPage will offer subscribers free services for four months when they start operation on April 1, sources say.
- FJ Benjamin general manager Wong Ai Fong says the company did not "mislead" investors on its performance in the run-up to its listing.
- London-based Consensus Economics Inc predicts Singapore's economic growth in the fourth quarter this year will hit a 9.1 percent high.
- Inchcape Bhd is seeking a separate listing for its marketing services division, a move it said was aimed at sharpening management focus and improving growth prospects.

- The Singapore dollar enjoyed its largest one-day rise in a year against the US dollar on news that Brunei will not sever its one-to-one currency agreement as well as Finance Minister Richard Hu's weekend speech to economists
- Douglas Ooi Thean Seng will soon step down as managing director of Kim Eng Securities to step down from company.

- Developer First Capital Corp plans to erect a bigger building on its Robinson Road site, it said after announcing a hefty 62 percent jump in interim group net profits for the period ending December 31.

- Electronic sub-contractor Venture Manufacturing has again surprised the market with better than expected results, but its accelerating growth and big drop in margins are starting to become worrying.
- Lion Asiapac, a Singapore-based unit of the Lion Group, will be acquiring a 50 percent stake in a major motorcycle maker in China for S$48.8 million.
